title: Graphic Designer Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your graphic designer salary from hourly rates under the Graphic Arts Award. Includes 38-hour week, fortnightly pay, tax, and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a graphic designer in Australia?
faqs.a: Under the Graphic Arts, Printing and Publishing Award 2020, a Level 5 graphic designer (trade certificate or Certificate III) earns $29.45 per hour as of 1 July 2026. Junior rates apply for those under 21, starting at 37.5% of Level 4 for under 17. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the hourly rate, making it $36.81 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly graphic designer rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,193.20. This assumes the same rate every week with no overtime or penalty rates. Fortnightly pay would be $1,119.10 × 2 = $2,238.20 before tax.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my graphic designer salary?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year). For a Level 5 graphic designer earning $58,193, your employer would contribute an additional $6,983.16 into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Graphic Designer Salary

If you work as a graphic designer in Australia, your pay is likely covered by the **Graphic Arts, Printing and Publishing Award 2020** (). This award sets minimum hourly rates for different classification levels, from entry-level to senior roles. Knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure helps you compare job offers, budget, and understand your tax obligations.

### The Award Rate for Graphic Designers

Under the award, a full-time adult graphic designer at **Level 5** (aligned with a trade certificate or Certificate III) earns **$29.45 per hour** as of 1 July 2026. That works out to **$1,119.10 per week** for 38 ordinary hours. If you are a junior (under 21), your rate is a percentage of the Level 4 rate – for example, a 20-year-old receives 87.5% of Level 4, which is $930.04 per week.

Casual employees get a **25% loading** on top of the hourly rate, making the casual rate $36.81 per hour. This loading is meant to compensate for the lack of paid leave. Always check your classification using the [pay guides](/blog) or the award itself.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time graphic designer at Level 5:

$29.45 × 38 × 52 = **$58,193.20 per year**

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. For example, a casual working 20 hours per week at $36.81 would earn $36.81 × 20 × 52 = $38,282.40 per year.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2:

$1,119.10 × 2 = **$2,238.20** (before tax and super).

This is useful for budgeting if you are paid on a fortnightly cycle.

### How Does This Compare to the National Minimum Wage?

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours (). This applies to award/agreement-free employees. A Level 5 graphic designer earns about $3.01 per hour more than the national minimum. Even the lowest award level (Level 1 at $25.74) is slightly below the national minimum, but award rates are generally higher for skilled roles.

### Tax on Your Graphic Designer Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners).

For a graphic designer earning $58,193:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: $26,800 × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $58,193: $13,193 × 30% = $3,957.90
- Total tax: $7,977.90
- Medicare levy: $58,193 × 2% = $1,163.86
- **Net annual pay: $58,193 – $7,977.90 – $1,163.86 = $49,051.24**

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more precise estimate.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **super guarantee** at **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a Level 5 graphic designer earning $58,193, the super contribution is **$6,983.16** per year. This is paid into your super fund and is not deducted from your salary. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Casual Loading and Annual Pay

If you are a casual graphic designer, remember that your hourly rate already includes the 25% loading. When converting to annual, use the loaded rate. For example, $36.81 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $72,736.56 per year. However, casuals do not receive paid leave, so your actual take-home may be higher per hour but less stable. Learn more about [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Using the Award to Check Your Rate

The Fair Work Ombudsman provides the full award and [reference tables](/data) for all classifications. If you are unsure which level applies to your role, check the classification definitions in the award. The **Modern Awards Pay Database** () contains the latest rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

### Final Thoughts

Your graphic designer salary depends on your award classification, experience, and whether you are full-time, part-time, or casual. The formula hourly × 38 × 52 gives a reliable annual estimate for full-time work. Remember that super is extra, and tax is progressive. For a quick calculation, try our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool. And always check the award or your enterprise agreement for the exact rate that applies to you.
